"'''Take Me Home, Country Roads'''", also known simply as "'''Country Roads'''", is a song written by [[Bill Danoff]], [[Taffy Nivert]], and [[John Denver]]. Denver released it as a single on April 12, 1971, and the song peaked at number two on [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard''{{'}}s US Hot 100 singles chart]] for the week ending August 28. "Take Me Home, Country Roads" was a success on its initial release and was certified gold by the RIAA on August 18, 1971, and platinum on April 10, 2017.{{Certification Cite Ref |artist=John Denver |title=Take Me Home, Country Road |region=United States |type=single}} It became one of Denver's most popular songs and has continued to sell, with over 1.8 million digital copies sold in the United States.<ref name="chartbeat">{{cite magazine|last=Trust|first=Gary|title=John Denver Back in Hot 100's Top 40 as a Writer Thanks to MGK & Jelly Roll's 'Lonely Road|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/chart-beat/john-denver-hot-100-top-40-jelly-roll-machine-gun-kelly-lonely-road-1235746767/|magazine=Billboard|date=August 5, 2024|access-date=August 5, 2024}}</ref>

The song has become a popular symbol of [[West Virginia]], which is mentioned in the very first verse. In March 2014, it became one of four of the state's [[List of U.S. state songs#State songs|official anthems]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 7, 2014 |title="Take Me Home Country Roads" |url=https://statesymbolsusa.org/take-me-home-country-roads |access-date=June 28, 2023 |website=State Symbols USA |language=en}}</ref>

Denver's 1971 recording was inducted into the [[Grammy Hall of Fame]] in 1998,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/hall-of-fame-award#t|title=GRAMMY Hall Of Fame Award|website=grammy.com}}</ref> and was selected by the [[Library of Congress]] for inclusion in the [[National Recording Registry]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023: National Recording Preservation Board |url=https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-recording-preservation-board/recording-registry/registry-by-induction-years/2023/ |access-date=June 28, 2023 |website=Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. 20540 USA}}</ref>

"Take Me Home, Country Roads", also known simply as "Country Roads", is a song written by Bill Danoff, Taffy Nivert, and John Denver. Denver released it as a single on April 12, 1971, and the song peaked at number two on Billboard{{'}}s US Hot 100 singles chart for the week ending August 28. "Take Me Home, Country Roads" was a success on its initial release and was certified gold by the RIAA on August 18, 1971, and platinum on April 10, 2017.{{Certification Cite Ref |artist=John Denver |title=Take Me Home, Country Road |region=United States |type=single}} It became one of Denver's most popular songs and has continued to sell, with over 1.8 million digital copies sold in the United States.

The song has become a popular symbol of West Virginia, which is mentioned in the very first verse. In March 2014, it became one of four of the state's official anthems.

Denver's 1971 recording was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame in 1998, and was selected by the Library of Congress for inclusion in the National Recording Registry in 2023.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext:
Inspiration for the title line had come while Taffy Nivert and Bill Danoff, who were married, were driving along [[Maryland Route 117|Clopper Road]] in [[Montgomery County, Maryland]], to a gathering of Nivert's family in [[Gaithersburg, Maryland|Gaithersburg]], with Nivert behind the wheel while Danoff played his guitar. Danoff stated: "I just started thinking, country roads, I started thinking of me growing up in western [[New England]] and going on all these small roads. It didn't have anything to do with Maryland or anyplace."<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Co-Writer of 'Take Me Home, Country Roads' Dispels Myths Surrounding Song's Origins|url=https://www.nbcwashington.com/news/local/co-writer-of-take-me-home-country-roads-dispels-myths-surrounding-songs-origins/2525010/?_osource=db_npd_nbc_wrc_eml_shr|last=Segraves|first=Mark|date=December 30, 2020|website=NBC4 Washington|access-date=August 30, 2021}}</ref>

To Danoff, the lyric "the radio reminds me of my home far away" in the bridge is quintessentially West Virginian, an allusion to when he listened to the program ''[[Wheeling Jamboree|Saturday Night Jamboree]]'', broadcast from [[Wheeling, West Virginia]], on [[WWVA (AM)|WWVA]] at his home in Springfield, Massachusetts, during his childhood in the 1950s.<ref name="WVUS">{{cite web|url=https://wvusports.com/news/2014/1/29/24994_131465976649784385.aspx?path=general |title=Take Me Home, Country Roads|publisher=WVUSports.com |date=January 29, 2014|access-date=February 11, 2019}}</ref>

Danoff was influenced by friend and West Virginian actor [[Chris Sarandon]] and members of a West Virginia commune who attended Danoff's performances.<ref name="WVUS" /> Of the commune members, Danoff remarked, "They brought their dogs and were a very colorful group of folks, but that is how West Virginia began creeping into the song." While the song was inspired by Danoff's upbringing in Springfield, Massachusetts, he "didn't want to write about Massachusetts because [he] didn't think the word was musical."<ref name="WVUS" />

Starting on December 22, 1970, Denver was heading the New Year's bill at [[The Cellar Door]] in Washington, D.C., with [[Starland Vocal Band|Fat City]] (which consisted of Nivert and Danoff) opening for him, just as Denver had opened at the same club for then-headliner [[David Steinberg]]. After the club's post-Christmas reopening night on Tuesday, December 29 (Cellar Door engagements ran from Tuesday to Sunday, and this booking was for two weeks), the three returned to the couple's apartment for an impromptu jam. On the way, Denver's left thumb was broken in a collision. He was rushed to the emergency room, where the thumb was splinted. When they returned to the apartment, Denver said he was "wired, you know."<ref>{{cite web |title="Take Me Home, Country Roads" |url=https://www.superseventies.com/1971_8singles.html |website=superseventies.com |access-date=April 5, 2022}}</ref>

When Danoff and Nivert ran through what they had of the song they had been working on for about a month, planning to sell to [[Johnny Cash]], Denver decided he had to have it, which prompted them to abandon plans for the sale.<ref>{{cite web |title=Footage Shows Johnny Cash Joining John Denver For 'Country Roads' Duet |url=https://classiccountrymusic.com/footage-shows-johnny-cash-joining-john-denver-for-country-roads-duet/ |website=classiccountrymusic.com |date=November 9, 2018 |publisher=Classic Country Music |access-date=April 5, 2022}}</ref> The verses and chorus were still missing a bridge, so the three of them went about finishing.

Nivert got out an encyclopedia to learn more about West Virginia. The first thing she encountered was the [[rhododendron]], the state flower, so she kept trying to work the word rhododendron into the song. "Rhododendron" was the title that Nivert had written down on the lyric sheet, which they later sent to [[American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers|ASCAP]].<ref name="WVUS" /> The three stayed up until 6:00 a.m., changing words and moving lines around.<ref name="Collis 22">{{cite book|last=Collis|first=John|title=John Denver: Mother Nature's Son|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BMuu7GKGIi4C&pg=PT22|date=September 30, 2011|publisher=Mainstream Publishing|isbn=978-1-78057-330-4|page=22}}</ref>

When they finished on the morning of December 30, 1970, the day before Denver's 27th birthday, he announced that the song had to go on his next album.<ref name="Collis 22" /> Later that night, during Denver's first set, Denver called his two collaborators back to the spotlight, where the trio changed their career trajectories, reading the lyrics from a single, handheld, unfolded piece of paper. According to Len Jaffe, a Washington, DC-based singer-songwriter who attended the show where Denver premiered the song, this resulted in a five-minute standing ovation.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Augenstein |first1=Neal |title=Real story behind 'Take Me Home, Country Roads'; debut 50 years ago in DC club |url=https://wtop.com/dc/2020/12/real-story-behind-take-me-home-country-roads-debut-50-years-ago-in-dc-club/ |website=wtop.com |date=December 21, 2020 |publisher=WTOP |access-date=April 5, 2022}}</ref> They recorded it in New York City in January 1971.

"Take Me Home, Country Roads" is written in the [[Key (music)|key]] of [[A major]] with a tempo of 82 [[beats per minute]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Find the BPM and key for any song |url=https://songbpm.com/@john-denver/take-me-home-country-roads |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309001328/https://songbpm.com/@john-denver/take-me-home-country-roads |archive-date=March 9, 2023 |access-date=March 8, 2023 |website=songbpm.com}}</ref>

sections.heading: Commercial performance and legacy
sections.wikitext:
"Take Me Home, Country Roads" appeared on the LP ''[[Poems, Prayers & Promises]]'' and was released as a [[Single (music)#7-inch format|45]] in the spring of 1971. Original pressings credited the single to "John Denver with Fat City". It broke nationally in mid-April, but moved up the charts very slowly.{{citation needed|date=August 2023}} The single reached number one on the ''[[Record World]]'' Pop Singles Chart and the [[Cash Box Top 100|''Cash Box'' Top 100]], and number two on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], topped only by "[[How Can You Mend a Broken Heart]]" by [[the Bee Gees]].

On August 18, 1971, the song was certified Gold by the RIAA for a million copies shipped.<ref name="RIAA" /> It continued to sell in the digital era, and as of January 2020, the song has also sold 1,800,000 downloads since it became available digitally.<ref name="chartbeat"/>

Denver's recording of "Take Me Home, Country Roads" was selected by the [[Library of Congress]] for preservation in the [[National Recording Registry]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web |title=2023 National Recording Registry selections |url=https://www.loc.gov/programs/national-recording-preservation-board/recording-registry/registry-by-induction-years/2023/ |website=Library of Congress |access-date=April 12, 2023}}</ref>

The song has become popular at sporting events, including games of the [[Brisbane Lions]] [[Australian rules football]] club,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Walsh |first1=Courtney |title=Humility a common thread as Lions rise from rock bottom to AFL grand final|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2023/sep/29/afl-grand-final-2023-brisbane-lions-rise-from-rock-bottom |access-date=October 31, 2023 |work=The Guardian |publisher=The Guardian Australia |date=September 29, 2023}}</ref> [[NFL International Series]] games held in [[Germany]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Thakur |first1=Anshu |title=Fans In Berlin Took Over The NFL Broadcast With 'Country Roads.' It Turned The Whole Stadium Into A Concert And Became The Night’s Biggest Highlight |url=https://www.operationsports.com/fans-in-berlin-took-over-the-nfl-broadcast-with-country-roads-it-turned-the-whole-stadium-into-a-concert-and-became-the-nights-biggest-highlight/ |access-date=May 7, 2026 |work=Operation Sports |publisher=GAMURS Group |date=November 10, 2025}}</ref> the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States national soccer team]]'s games,<ref name="TG 2026">{{Cite web |title=Take me home: why Country Roads has struck a chord at the World Cup |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/20/take-me-home-country-roads-world-cup-usmnt |last=Rueter |first=Jeff |date=2026-06-20 |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] games.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Why we play 'Country Roads' before kick-off|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/bruno-fernandes-explains-decision-to-play-country-roads-before-old-trafford-kickoffs|website=www.manutd.com|access-date=|language=en|date=2025-04-17}}</ref>

The song was interpolated in "[[Lonely Road (Machine Gun Kelly and Jelly Roll song)|Lonely Road]]" by [[Machine Gun Kelly (musician)|Machine Gun Kelly]] and [[Jelly Roll (singer)|Jelly Roll]] in 2024. It reached number 33 on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 chart dated August 10, 2024, giving Denver his first top-40 appearance as a songwriter since the same song's appearance in the medley "[[Forever Country]]" by Artists of Then, Now & Forever peaked at number 21 in 2016.<ref name="chartbeat"/>

It broke nationally in mid-April, but moved up the charts very slowly.{{citation needed|date=August 2023}} The single reached number one on the Record World Pop Singles Chart and the Cash Box Top 100, and number two on the US Billboard Hot 100, topped only by "How Can You Mend a Broken Heart" by the Bee Gees.

On August 18, 1971, the song was certified Gold by the RIAA for a million copies shipped. It continued to sell in the digital era, and as of January 2020, the song has also sold 1,800,000 downloads since it became available digitally.

Denver's recording of "Take Me Home, Country Roads" was selected by the Library of Congress for preservation in the National Recording Registry in 2023.

The song has become popular at sporting events, including games of the Brisbane Lions Australian rules football club, NFL International Series games held in Germany, the United States national soccer team's games, and Manchester United games.

It reached number 33 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart dated August 10, 2024, giving Denver his first top-40 appearance as a songwriter since the same song's appearance in the medley "Forever Country" by Artists of Then, Now & Forever peaked at number 21 in 2016.

"Take Me Home, Country Roads" received an enthusiastic response from West Virginians.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://expatalachians.com/country-roads-how-john-denvers-hit-became-the-worlds-most-popular-song |title='Country Roads:' How John Denver's Hit Became the World's Most Popular Song |last=Brumfield |first=Nick |date=March 5, 2019 |website=Expatalachians |access-date=April 17, 2022}}</ref> On November 1, 2017, the West Virginia Tourism Office announced it had obtained the rights to use "Take Me Home, Country Roads" in its marketing efforts. West Virginia Tourism Commissioner Chelsea Ruby stated: {{"'}}Country Roads' has become synonymous with West Virginia all over the world. It highlights everything we love about our state: scenic beauty, majestic mountains, a timeless way of life, and most of all, the warmth of a place that feels like home whether you've lived here forever or are just coming to visit." The opening phrase of the song, "Almost heaven", became a primary tourism office slogan.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 1, 2017 |title=WV Tourism obtains rights to use John Denver's 'Take Me Home, Country Roads' |url=https://wvpress.org/breaking-news/wv-tourism-obtains-rights-use-john-denvers-take-home-country-roads |access-date=December 1, 2018 |publisher=West Virginia Press}}</ref>

The song is the theme song of [[West Virginia University]], and it has been performed during every home football pregame show since 1972. The song is also played after every home victory and fans are encouraged to stay in the stands and sing along with the team. It is also played for other athletic events and university functions.<ref>{{cite web |date=November 3, 2009 |title=Welcome To | WVU Traditions | West Virginia University |url=http://welcometo.wvu.edu/living_here/wvu_traditions |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720121918/http://welcometo.wvu.edu/living_here/wvu_traditions |archive-date=July 20, 2011 |access-date=January 29, 2011 |publisher=Welcometo.wvu.edu}}</ref> On September 6, 1980, at the invitation of West Virginia Governor [[Jay Rockefeller]], songwriters Danoff, Nivert, and Denver performed the song during pregame festivities to a sold-out crowd at the opening of [[Mountaineer Field at Milan Puskar Stadium|Mountaineer Field]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Country Roads-John Denver WVU 1980 Introduction and Full Song (Audio)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Plndo6Rie7E| archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211107/Plndo6Rie7E| archive-date=November 7, 2021 | url-status=live|via=YouTube|access-date=December 1, 2018|date=July 8, 2013|quote=John Denver, Bill Danoff, and Taffy Nivert performing "Take Me Home, Country Roads" at the opening of West Virginia University's Mountaineer Field September 6, 1980. This audio recording includes the introduction by John Denver followed by the full song as recorded by WVAQ with Jack Fleming announcing.}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

The popularity of the song inspired resolutions in the [[West Virginia Legislature]] to adopt "Take Me Home, Country Roads" as an official [[List of U.S. state songs|state song]]. On March 7, 2014, the West Virginia Legislature approved a resolution to make "Take Me Home, Country Roads" an official state song of West Virginia, alongside three other pieces: "West Virginia Hills", "This Is My West Virginia", and "West Virginia, My Home Sweet Home".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wvgazette.com/News/201403070150 |title=W.Va. Takes home 'Country Roads' |newspaper=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]] |access-date=March 16, 2014 |date=March 7, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140316212401/http://www.wvgazette.com/News/201403070150 |archive-date=March 16, 2014}}</ref> The next day, governor [[Earl Ray Tomblin]] signed the resolution into law.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wchstv.com/newsroom/eyewitness/140307_23786.shtml |title= "Country Roads" To Become Fourth Official West Virginia State Song |access-date=March 7, 2014 |date=March 7, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140308010234/http://www.wchstv.com/newsroom/eyewitness/140307_23786.shtml |work=[[WCHS-TV]] |archive-date=March 8, 2014}}</ref>

The song was played at the funeral for West Virginia Senator [[Robert Byrd]] at the [[West Virginia State Capitol|state capitol]] in Charleston, West Virginia, on July 2, 2010.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Garcia |first=Jon |date=July 2, 2010 |title=Eulogizing Sen. Robert Byrd: The Hard Working, if Imperfect, Senator |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |url=http://blogs.abcnews.com/politicalpunch/2010/07/eulogizing-sen-robert-byrd-the-hard-working-if-imperfect-senator.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100705104518/http://blogs.abcnews.com/politicalpunch/2010/07/eulogizing-sen-robert-byrd-the-hard-working-if-imperfect-senator.html |archive-date=July 5, 2010}}</ref>

The song is the theme song of West Virginia University, and it has been performed during every home football pregame show since 1972. The song is also played after every home victory and fans are encouraged to stay in the stands and sing along with the team. It is also played for other athletic events and university functions. On September 6, 1980, at the invitation of West Virginia Governor Jay Rockefeller, songwriters Danoff, Nivert, and Denver performed the song during pregame festivities to a sold-out crowd at the opening of Mountaineer Field.

The popularity of the song inspired resolutions in the West Virginia Legislature to adopt "Take Me Home, Country Roads" as an official state song. On March 7, 2014, the West Virginia Legislature approved a resolution to make "Take Me Home, Country Roads" an official state song of West Virginia, alongside three other pieces: "West Virginia Hills", "This Is My West Virginia", and "West Virginia, My Home Sweet Home". The next day, governor Earl Ray Tomblin signed the resolution into law.

The song was played at the funeral for West Virginia Senator Robert Byrd at the state capitol in Charleston, West Virginia, on July 2, 2010.

sections.heading: ''Fallout 76'' version
sections.wikitext: A cover version of the song, a collaboration between [[COPILOT Music and Sound|Copilot Music and Sound]] and the vocal group Spank,<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hines |first1=Pete |title=IT'S FINALLY HERE. Download Country Roads cover now. It was recorded by our friends at CoPilot with a group out of New York called Spank. You've never heard of them, but maybe seen them performing on the streets of New York. |url=https://twitter.com/DCDeacon/status/1014506153785659394 |website=Twitter |access-date=March 2, 2021 |language=en |date=July 4, 2018}}</ref> was commissioned for and featured in both the teaser and full [[Electronic Entertainment Expo 2018|E3 2018]] trailers for the 2018 video game ''[[Fallout 76]]'', with its plot events set in West Virginia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.polygon.com/e3/2018/6/11/17449092/fallout-76-song-john-denver-country-roads |title=Fallout 76 has everyone humming John Denver |last=Kuchera |first=Ben |date=June 11, 2018 |access-date=July 22, 2018 |work=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |publisher=[[Vox Media, Inc.]]}}</ref> Released as an iTunes-only single on July 4, 2018, the song reached No. 1 on the iTunes singles chart.<ref name="Variety">{{cite news |last1=Hampp |first1=Andrew |title=Songs for Screens: How a John Denver Classic Resurfaced Thanks to 'Fallout 76' |url=https://variety.com/2018/music/news/songs-for-screens-how-a-john-denver-classic-resurfaced-thanks-to-fallout-76-1202891172/#! |access-date=September 17, 2018 |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=July 31, 2018}}</ref> It debuted at No. 41 on ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard's]]'' [[Hot Country Songs]] chart that week and at No. 21 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Country Digital Songs the following week.<ref name="Variety" /> The official YouTube upload of the original John Denver recording, initially uploaded in 2013, would later edit its description in response to the song's use for the game.<ref>{{cite web|title=John Denver – Take Me Home, Country Roads (Audio)|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vrEljMfXYo|via=YouTube|access-date=October 11, 2018|date=April 5, 2013|quote=John Denver's official audio for 'Take Me Home, Country Roads', as featured on Fallout 76.}}</ref> In Australia, a promotional ''Fallout 76'' [[Phonograph record|vinyl]] featuring the cover was included with the December 2018 issue of ''STACK Magazine'' exclusively from retailer [[JB Hi-Fi]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://stack.com.au/games/games-news/grab-a-free-fallout-76-vinyl-with-this-months-stack-magazine/ |title=Grab a FREE Fallout 76 vinyl with this month's STACK Magazine |publisher=stack.com.au |first=Alesha |last=Kolbe |date=December 3, 2018 |access-date=December 4, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181205052821/https://stack.com.au/games/games-news/grab-a-free-fallout-76-vinyl-with-this-months-stack-magazine/ |archive-date=December 5, 2018}}</ref>
sections.text: A cover version of the song, a collaboration between Copilot Music and Sound and the vocal group Spank, was commissioned for and featured in both the teaser and full E3 2018 trailers for the 2018 video game Fallout 76, with its plot events set in West Virginia. Released as an iTunes-only single on July 4, 2018, the song reached No. 1 on the iTunes singles chart. It debuted at No. 41 on Billboard's Hot Country Songs chart that week and at No. 21 on Billboard{{'}}s Country Digital Songs the following week. The official YouTube upload of the original John Denver recording, initially uploaded in 2013, would later edit its description in response to the song's use for the game. In Australia, a promotional Fallout 76 vinyl featuring the cover was included with the December 2018 issue of STACK Magazine exclusively from retailer JB Hi-Fi.
